description: Queue an authenticated HTTP request using only the registered marketo_instance tenant and credential. Supply method (GET/POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE), a relative path such as /rest/v1/leads/delete.json, /rest/asset/v1/programs.json or /bulk/v1/activities/export/create.json, optional query, JSON object or form body and non-Authorization headers. Vendor RBAC is the operation boundary. Poll check_marketo_job_status(job_id) for the response.
embedding_description: Reach Marketo REST Lead Database, Assets, Bulk Extract/Import and Identity endpoints before a typed wrapper exists. Create, update, correct, clear, retire or delete using vendor semantics. Preserve HTTP status, response body, Marketo success/errors and nextPageToken, including rate-limit retry-after. Caller is responsible for vendor concurrency premises, lifecycle and pagination.

result_processor_customizations.result_description: Immediate job_id/status; completed job result contains status (HTTP), body (JSON or text), correlation_id, retry_after (nullable), and nextPageToken/success/errors when present in the vendor envelope. Credential fields and known credential values are redacted. No automatic retry of writes on HTTP errors or rate limits; one explicit expired-token envelope may refresh authentication.
result_processor_customizations.presentation_guidance: This call may have changed vendor state. A queued job is not vendor success. Poll check_marketo_job_status, then report HTTP status and body faithfully, including API success/errors and any nextPageToken/retry_after. Do not turn an HTTP 200 success:false into success. Preserve vendor terminal/job ids for subsequent polling with request; generic request does not itself manage a Bulk job lifecycle. Credentials are redacted, including identity access_token. Do not claim file upload support: this unit handles JSON and form bodies; typed file wrappers follow.

error_processor_customizations.action_context: Queue a Marketo request using registered credentials.
error_processor_customizations.error_interpretation: Dispatch shape/target errors occur before vendor I/O. A failed background job may have reached the vendor: do not retry a write automatically. HTTP 4xx/5xx and vendor error envelopes are returned as data, not suppressed. Inspect status, success/errors and retry_after. Only relative targets on the registered instance are accepted; Host cannot change and header values cannot contain CR/LF.
